audit_origin.note: Independent read-only audit at parent_head established that the frozen protocol entails unregistered-schema -> UNKNOWN_SCHEMA -> SCHEMA_MISMATCH -> fail-closed raw retention, but does NOT normatively entail unregistered-schema -> invalid/inadmissible DailyMarketEvidenceV1. This amendment closes exactly that gap and no other.

next_step: Parser B / materializer remediation (enforcing schema_admission_rule in validate_daily_market_evidence_v1 or an equivalent boundary check) against the now-candidate effective protocol is a required subsequent implementation task, per semantic_body.parser_status.parser_b_current.disposition. This candidate must itself be reviewed and frozen (self_freeze_authorized: false; no self-freeze performed here) before that remediation task treats it as authoritative. Any such remediation must thread registry_snapshot_sha256 explicitly through the admission decision per semantic_body.registry_snapshot_binding -- it must not resolve the registry implicitly from a live file read.

repair_history.change_summary: Replaced wall-clock 'known_schema_variants ... at the time of evaluation' semantics in schema_admission_rule with an explicit, caller-supplied registry_snapshot_sha256 binding (new semantic_body.registry_snapshot_binding section) and tightened raw_scientific_firewall.later_registration_does_not_silently_reinterpret_frozen_inputs to reference it. No change to which raw-bytes/registered-schema/raw-retention/duplicate/lifecycle/PIT/outcome semantics this amendment governs or declares out of scope; no code (Parser A, Parser B, materializer) modified; no field added to DailyMarketEvidenceV1.

Replaced independently caller-supplied known_schema_variants plus registry_snapshot_sha256 with one exact-byte registry-artifact snapshot input from which both variants and sha256 identity are mechanically derived; added the minimum canonical durable X/R/C/D evaluation receipt requirement. No Parser A, Parser B, materializer, DailyMarketEvidenceV1, retention, lifecycle, assignment, duplicate, funding, PIT, or outcome semantics changed.

Hardened the executable reference/conformance model so RegistrySnapshot accepts exact registry artifact bytes only and re-derives membership plus R from those bytes at evaluation; GoverningRule derives C only after verifying the amendment and its named base-contract/base-registry bytes; added durable receipt verification that recomputes X/R/C/schema/D from supplied authority and rejects a mismatched receipt. No Parser A, Parser B, materializer, DailyMarketEvidenceV1, retention, lifecycle, assignment, duplicate, funding, PIT, or outcome semantics changed.

amends.how_to_read: effective_contract = original r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json (unmodified) PLUS original r1_source_schema_registry_v1.json (unmodified) PLUS this amendment. Neither original artifact's bytes are edited by this amendment; both remain the historical record of what was (under-)specified before this amendment. This artifact does not retroactively imply the resolved rule existed at freeze time.
target_fields_amended: DailyMarketEvidenceV1 (record-level: adds a new normative admission rule; does not alter any individual field's existing type, missingness, or precision spec)

impossible_state.reproduced_prior_countermodel: The auditor's exact countermodel (schema_id=UNKNOWN_SCHEMA, SCHEMA_MISMATCH present, raw retained, record otherwise complete, status=MATERIALIZED_VALID, is_valid=true) is now a direct violation of schema_admission_rule.rule under this amendment: condition (b) fails (schema_id is not a known_schema_variants key), so the record is SCHEMA_INADMISSIBLE by definition, contradicting is_valid=true. The countermodel remains constructible in the CURRENT, unmodified Parser B implementation (see underspecification_recorded.empirical_corroboration_not_itself_the_gap) -- that implementation gap is exactly why parser_status.parser_b_current below records NONCONFORMING; remediating it is the required subsequent implementation task, not part of this amendment.
impossible_state.statement: Under this amendment, the state {schema_id NOT IN known_schema_variants (or schema_id is None/UNKNOWN_SCHEMA)} AND {record is SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE (or otherwise treated as a valid, admitted DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record)} is a direct contradiction of schema_admission_rule.rule condition (b), which is a conjunctive necessary condition for admission. No combination of field-completeness, raw retention, or any other pre-existing contract condition can satisfy admission when (b) fails, because schema_admission_rule.rule requires (a) AND (b), not (a) OR (b).

registered_schema_does_not_imply_valid.statement: Under this amendment, {schema_id IN known_schema_variants} does NOT by itself imply {record is a valid/admitted DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record}. Condition (a) -- every other pre-existing, already-frozen requirement -- still applies in full and independently; a record can satisfy (b) and still fail (a) (e.g. a registered-schema record missing a required non-null field when trade_count>0 remains inadmissible under that pre-existing rule, unaffected by this amendment).

explicitly_not_addressed_by_this_amendme: malformed-row / PARSE_REJECTION dispositions unrelated to schema identity
which known_schema_variants entries exist or should exist (registry membership itself is untouched -- see amends.original_schema_registry_bytes_unchanged_by_this_amendment)
the exact code location/mechanism used to enforce schema_admission_rule (a required subsequent implementation task; see parser_status)
any R1 hypothesis, factor, weight, return, PnL, IC, or Sharpe computation
semantic_body.outcome_embargo_verified: no H012/H014, PIT rank, weight, forward return, PnL, IC, Sharpe, or weekly/null/replication outcome was computed, inspected, or referenced in producing this amendment

parser_a_current.reason: Parser A already never emits a non-None record for an unrecognized column set; every unknown-schema object already reaches materialize_parser_a's 'result.record is None' branch and is quarantined (MATERIALIZATION_QUARANTINED), never MATERIALIZED_VALID. This predates and is unmodified by this amendment; it already satisfies schema_admission_rule.

parser_b_current.conformance: NONCONFORMING (expected, not remediated by this amendment)
parser_b_current.disposition: This amendment is a protocol document; it deliberately does not modify Parser B, Parser A, or the materializer (no shared runtime recognition gate is implemented here). Remediating Parser B / the materializer's validate_daily_market_evidence_v1 to enforce schema_admission_rule is recorded here as a REQUIRED SUBSEQUENT IMPLEMENTATION STEP, to be performed and reviewed as its own task, mirroring parser_status.parser_a.disposition's convention in r1_normalized_evidence_duplicate_semantics_amendment_v1.json.
parser_b_current.reason: daily_primitive() appends SCHEMA_MISMATCH to its anomalies list on an unknown header but does not stop building a complete trade-count/OHLC/turnover record from the (still-parsed) rows, and validate_daily_market_evidence_v1 checks only required-key/non-null/type conditions -- never schema_id registry membership or the anomalies list -- so materialize_parser_b currently returns MaterializationResult(status=MATERIALIZED_VALID, is_valid=True, ...) for an unknown-schema object with parseable rows. This is exactly the countermodel this amendment closes at the protocol level.

raw_scientific_firewall.firewall_statement: RAW RETENTION != SCIENTIFIC ADMISSION. This distinction, already established for the broader raw-retention scope candidate (r1_global_raw_retention_scope_candidate_v1.json:firewall_invariants, 'RAW_RETAINED != STRUCTURALLY_REQUIRED != ASSIGNED != NORMALIZED != PIT_ELIGIBLE != STRATEGY_INPUT'), is extended by exactly one further link for the schema dimension this amendment governs: RAW_RETAINED != SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE. Nothing in that existing chain is edited; this amendment adds a link, it does not renumber or remove any existing one.
raw_scientific_firewall.later_registration_does_not_silently_rei: If a future, independently reviewed amendment establishes a new registry snapshot R2 (per registry_snapshot_binding.explicit_reevaluation_only) that registers a previously-unregistered schema variant, that registration is bound to R2 only: it does not, by itself or by any mechanism this amendment defines, alter a DailyMarketEvidenceV1 admission evaluation already recorded under a prior registry snapshot R1 (registry_snapshot_binding.no_silent_reclassification). Re-materializing the same raw bytes later does not implicitly pick up R2 in place of R1; a fresh evaluation under R2 is a distinct, separately identified evaluation (registry_snapshot_binding.evaluation_identity), never a rewrite of the R1 evaluation. This mirrors the existing, unedited convention already established by r1_normalized_evidence_duplicate_semantics_amendment_v1.json:amends.amendment_relationship (ADDITIVE_CLARIFICATION_NOT_IN_PLACE_REWRITE) and avoids treating raw-retained-but-unregistered evidence as a permanent, unrepairable dead end.
raw_scientific_firewall.retention_does_not_imply_assignment: Retaining an unknown-schema raw object does not assign it to any instrument_instance_id-scoped evidence population; assignment remains governed entirely by its own pre-existing, unmodified rules.
raw_scientific_firewall.retention_does_not_imply_dailymarket_adm: Retaining an unknown-schema raw object never, by itself or in combination with any other condition this amendment states, makes a DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record derived from it SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE. Only schema_id registry membership under the specific, explicitly identified registry snapshot R that governs a given evaluation does (schema_admission_rule.rule condition (b); registry_snapshot_binding).
raw_scientific_firewall.retention_does_not_imply_interpretation: An unknown-schema raw object being RAW_RETAINED (per r1_source_schema_registry_v1.json:policy's fail-closed raw retention) carries no implication about what, if anything, its bytes mean; this amendment does not authorize or require any interpretation of SCHEMA_INADMISSIBLE raw bytes.

evaluation_provenance.canonical_encoding: UTF-8 canonical JSON: json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True) plus one trailing newline; the durable receipt bytes themselves are the replayable value, not an in-memory Python object.
evaluation_provenance.disposition_determinism: For a fixed source_object_sha256 X, exact registry artifact bytes R, governing authority C, and schema_id, the schema-admission predicate is deterministic: a protocol-valid evaluation cannot record two different dispositions D. The receipt carries schema_id as the deterministic record-level input to the schema dimension; it does not make registration sufficient for overall DailyMarketEvidenceV1 validity.
evaluation_provenance.owner: A separate SCHEMA_ADMISSION_EVALUATION_RECEIPT_V1 provenance value associated with the existing raw-object/source receipt and materialized-record provenance. It is deliberately not a DailyMarketEvidenceV1 field and this candidate does not implement its runtime storage location; the subsequent Parser B/materializer remediation must emit, durably retain, and verify it before treating an evaluation as valid.
evaluation_provenance.replay_requirement: A PARSED_RECEIPT is only canonical JSON with the required fields. A VERIFIED_SCHEMA_ADMISSION_EVALUATION requires the receipt plus the supplied upstream source-object identity X, exact registry artifact bytes, and governing amendment/base-contract/base-registry artifact bytes: the verifier MUST derive R=sha256(exact registry bytes), parse membership only from those same bytes, derive and verify C from the governing authority, recompute D for the receipt schema_id, and reject unless every claimed X/R/C/D value matches. On process exit, only this authority-backed replay establishes a valid recorded evaluation; a frozen Python dataclass or deserialized receipt alone is not one.

registry_snapshot_binding.binding_authority_reused: This repair uses the existing sha256-artifact-pinning convention exactly as bound_authority.base_registry_sha256 does: R is SHA-256 of the exact registry artifact bytes, not a canonicalized parsed map, semantic-body hash, or a caller assertion. No field is added to DailyMarketEvidenceV1 and no code (Parser A, Parser B, or the materializer) is modified by this repair.
registry_snapshot_binding.closes: Independent hostile review verdict BLOCK_REGISTRY_TIME_AMBIGUITY on this amendment's pre-repair content (schema_admission_rule previously read known_schema_variants 'at the time of evaluation', a live/wall-clock-dependent read with no per-decision registry-version binding).
registry_snapshot_binding.determinism_requirement: admission(X, R, C, schema_id, t1) == admission(X, R, C, schema_id, t2) for all execution times t1, t2. The predicate accepts one explicit immutable registry artifact snapshot whose only authoritative input is exact bytes and derives both known_schema_variants and registry_snapshot_sha256=sha256(exact_artifact_bytes) from them; it never accepts independently asserted membership or R and never reads an ambient/current registry. Any future implementation MUST thread this snapshot object or its exact bytes end to end and MUST NOT resolve it implicitly from a live registry path.
registry_snapshot_binding.does_not_foreclose_future_registration: This binding requirement does not prevent a future amendment from registering a previously-unknown schema variant, and does not make raw-retained-but-currently-unregistered evidence a permanent dead end (see raw_scientific_firewall.unknown_schema_raw_bytes_may_remain_retained); it only requires that admitting evidence under a newly-registered variant happen via an explicit, separately identified R2 evaluation rather than an implicit, wall-clock-triggered reinterpretation of the R1 evaluation.
registry_snapshot_binding.evaluation_identity: An admission evaluation is uniquely identified by the triple (source_object_sha256 X of the raw object being evaluated, registry_snapshot_sha256 R mechanically derived from the exact registry artifact bytes whose known_schema_variants governed it, and governing_effective_combined_contract_binding_sha256 C). Its canonical durable receipt additionally records schema_id and resulting disposition D as evaluation_provenance requires. Two evaluations sharing X/R/C are the same protocol evaluation and MUST have the same D; a different C is a different identity even if X and R match.
registry_snapshot_binding.explicit_reevaluation_only: Admission of the same raw bytes under a later-registered schema is obtainable only via an explicit NEW evaluation that itself names and hashes its own governing registry snapshot R2 (a distinct registry artifact produced by its own explicit, independently reviewed future amendment -- consistent with this repository's existing versioning convention of new artifacts/amendments rather than in-place edits of already-referenced bytes, e.g. r1_source_precedence.json -> r1_source_precedence_freeze.json, r1_daily_market_materialization_boundary_v1/v2/v3, r1_instance_domain_manifest_v1/v2). That new evaluation is bound to R2, is a separate recorded fact from the R1 evaluation, and never causes the R1 evaluation's own stored disposition to change.
registry_snapshot_binding.no_silent_reclassification: An admission evaluation already recorded in its canonical durable receipt under registry_snapshot_sha256=R1 is immutable: it MUST NOT be overwritten, replaced, or silently reinterpreted by re-running materialization on the same raw bytes at a later time. A registry artifact with different bytes has a different R by construction; it is never an in-place R1 mutation. A change in registry state is never grounds to alter a previously recorded R1 evaluation in place.
registry_snapshot_binding.snapshot_construction: RegistrySnapshot(exact_artifact_bytes) is the normative input shape: parse known_schema_variants only from those bytes and derive registry_snapshot_sha256=sha256(exact_artifact_bytes) as properties, never caller-supplied fields. The evaluator re-constructs the snapshot from exact_artifact_bytes before use and therefore never trusts cached or substituted membership/R state. Thus R1 bytes/hash plus R2 membership, and the reverse, are rejected or collapse to the membership actually parsed from the supplied bytes; changing even one artifact byte produces a distinct R.

schema_admission_rule.no_automatic_validity_from_registration: SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE (condition (b) holding) does not itself make a record valid or admitted. Every other already-frozen DailyMarketEvidenceV1 requirement -- required-key presence, required-non-null conditions (including the trade_count=0 null exceptions), decimal-string precision_semantics, and the duplicate-semantics amendment's row-order-non-interference and representative-selection rules -- continues to apply unchanged and independently. A record with a registered schema_id that violates any of those pre-existing rules remains inadmissible under the pre-existing rule that it violates; this amendment neither weakens nor bypasses any of them. This holds independently under every registry snapshot R: no R makes condition (a) unnecessary, and re-evaluating under a different R never relaxes condition (a).
schema_admission_rule.predicate_definition: daily_market_evidence_v1_schema_admission(source_object_sha256, schema_id, registry_snapshot, governing_rule) -> SchemaAdmissionEvaluation. registry_snapshot has exact registry artifact bytes as its sole authoritative input; the evaluator re-derives both known_schema_variants and R=sha256(exact bytes) before membership evaluation. governing_rule has governing amendment/base-contract/base-registry artifact bytes as its authority inputs; the evaluator re-verifies their named hashes, amendment semantic hash, and effective binding before deriving C. The predicate is pure and reads neither a live registry nor ambient/current state. Returns SCHEMA_INADMISSIBLE if schema_id is None or absent from snapshot-derived membership; otherwise SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE. It emits canonical X/R/C/D receipt bytes. verify_schema_admission_evaluation(receipt, supplied_X, registry_bytes, governing_artifacts) is required to establish a VERIFIED_SCHEMA_ADMISSION_EVALUATION by independently recomputing and matching every claimed X/R/C/schema_id/D value. This governs only the schema dimension and remains necessary, not sufficient.
schema_admission_rule.rule: A candidate DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record is SCIENTIFICALLY_ADMISSIBLE under a given, explicitly identified registry snapshot R (R = the sha256 of one specific registry artifact's bytes -- e.g. r1_source_schema_registry_v1.json at base_registry_sha256, or a future amendment's own successor registry artifact, named and hashed by that amendment) only if both of the following hold: (a) it satisfies every pre-existing, already-frozen required-key / required-non-null / missingness / type condition stated in r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json:DailyMarketEvidenceV1 for each of its own fields (this amendment restates none of those conditions and relaxes none of them, under any R), AND (b) its schema_id names an entry present in known_schema_variants AS THEY EXISTED IN REGISTRY SNAPSHOT R (i.e. schema_id is not UNKNOWN_SCHEMA and the record does not carry a SCHEMA_MISMATCH disposition, evaluated against R and only R). A record for which (b) does not hold under R is SCHEMA_INADMISSIBLE-UNDER-R and MUST NOT be treated as a valid or admitted DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record by any consumer under R, regardless of whether (a) holds. Every admission evaluation MUST record which R governed it (registry_snapshot_sha256); a disposition recorded without an explicit, bound R is not a valid evaluation under this rule. See registry_snapshot_binding for the determinism and no-silent-reclassification requirements this implies.
schema_admission_rule.why_minimum_vocabulary: SCHEMA_ADMISSIBLE/SCHEMA_INADMISSIBLE, RegistrySnapshot, registry_snapshot_sha256, and SCHEMA_ADMISSION_EVALUATION_RECEIPT_V1 are the only new terms this repair adds. The receipt is the minimum owner for durable X/R/C/D provenance without mutating DailyMarketEvidenceV1; it reuses existing source_object_sha256 and exact-byte sha256 artifact-pinning conventions.

underspecification_recorded.empirical_corroboration_not_itself_the_g: This amendment is a protocol-text gap, not a code bug report. It is empirically corroborated (not established) by the fact that the current, unmodified Parser B path already exhibits exactly this countermodel: qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.daily_primitive continues to build a complete trade-count/OHLC/turnover record and append SCHEMA_MISMATCH to its anomalies list when schema_identify() returns schema_known=False (qntylab/r1_retention_candidate.py:149-152), and qntylab.r1_daily_market_materializer.validate_daily_market_evidence_v1 never inspects schema_id or the anomalies list, so materialize_parser_b returns MaterializationResult(status=MATERIALIZED_VALID, is_valid=True, ...) for such a record today. Parser A's own STATUS_UNKNOWN_SCHEMA_QUARANTINE path (record=None on unknown schema) independently corroborates that fail-closed non-admission for unknown schema is the evident engineering intent, not that it was ever written down as a normative DailyMarketEvidenceV1-layer rule binding on every implementation path. See parser_status below; this amendment does not modify either parser or the materializer -- it makes the rule normative so that Parser B's current behavior becomes a documented, reviewable nonconformance rather than an undetectable protocol gap.
underspecification_recorded.explicit_statement: As written prior to this amendment, the frozen contract and schema registry establish that an unregistered/unmatched source-schema variant is UNKNOWN_SCHEMA and triggers SCHEMA_MISMATCH with fail-closed RAW retention (r1_source_schema_registry_v1.json:policy; r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json:DailyMarketEvidenceV1.schema_id.missingness_semantics), but neither artifact, nor any other frozen artifact reviewed for this amendment, states that UNKNOWN_SCHEMA/SCHEMA_MISMATCH makes the resulting DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record scientifically invalid or inadmissible. A countermodel in which schema_id=UNKNOWN_SCHEMA, SCHEMA_MISMATCH is present, raw bytes are retained, the record is otherwise field-complete, and the record is nonetheless treated as a valid, admitted DailyMarketEvidenceV1 violates no existing frozen rule text.
underspecification_recorded.gap: unregistered schema / UNKNOWN_SCHEMA does not normatively entail invalid or inadmissible DailyMarketEvidenceV1
